findings.title: claimBuilderFees is permissionless but strictly caller-scoped
findings.actor: any address with a nonzero builderFees entry of its own
findings.precondition: The set-2 Exchange maps builder fees at slot 39; the slot-39 idiom is absent from the pinned implementation (0 occurrences of PUSH1 0x27), so the mechanism is new.
findings.trigger: 0x69f9a5f0 claimBuilderFees() zeroes keccak256(abi.encode(msg.sender, 39)) and debits the shared slot-38 high 96 bits by that amount.
findings.impact: The claim is not access-controlled, but it can only touch the caller's own entry, so no caller can take another builder's accrual: with entries 5e18 for A and 7e18 for B, A's call pays exactly 5e18 and leaves B's entry intact, B's pays exactly 7e18, the shared slot-38 counter falls by exactly the two amounts, and an address with no entry succeeds and is paid zero. Cross-caller theft is therefore disproved; the fee is not a bearer asset. An amount larger than the slot-38 counter reverts with a checked-arithmetic panic. The only entry points that touch slot 39 in any driven shape are this one (caller key) and the owner reassignment 0xd970fad5; the sweep family, the close and the open leave it alone.
evidence: testExchangeClaimBuilderFeesIsPermissionlessSelfClaim (outsider pays out its own entry, entry zeroed, slot-38 high 96 bits -= the amount, event 0x3416b71e..., overdraw panics 0x4e487b71, zero entry is a no-op success)
peer exact-runtime rows L2-D2-04 in atlas/block_48902346/live2_intents.json (two seeded entries: each caller is paid only its own, the other survives)
peer exact-runtime rows L2-D1-06 and L2-D2-04 in atlas/block_48902346/live2_intents.json (sweep family, close and open all leave the seeded slot-39 entries untouched)
static: pinned Exchange PUSH1 0x27 count = 0; set2 count = 4
findings.missing_observation: Where the paid amount lands after the linked-library call (the Exchange balance mapping at base 9 was unchanged in the replay).

findings.title: The close's builder-fee credit keys on an unidentified memory word, and the close struct has no builder field
findings.actor: a closer (the credit site is inside the signed-close body)
findings.precondition: The signed-close struct is Close(address user,uint256[] positionIds,uint256 nonce,uint64 deadline): the CLOSE_TYPEHASH constant 0x9cc23a52... is byte-identical in the pinned and the set-2 Exchange runtime and hash-matches that signature, so no builder field is signed.
findings.trigger: A close that accrues a fee reaches the slot-39 credit site at 0x32b6: it loads a word from mload(args_base + 0x180), masks it to 160 bits, and does keccak256(., 39) -> SLOAD -> checked add -> SSTORE.
findings.impact: The credit site is real in the set-2 bytes, but the source of the keyed word is not identified: appending an unsigned 8th calldata word leaves the credited key and the Exchange write set unchanged, and a six-element positionIds array does not make any element the key. An empty or loss-free close writes nothing, so the block is only entered when a fee exists: four driven entry points (0x01681a62 sweep with and without a pending request, 0xe0189108 requestSweep, 0x6d142da1 finalizeSweep) all left seeded slot-39 entries untouched, so no non-fee-paying shape reaches the credit block, and my earlier lead that the helper block belongs to entry 0x01681a62 is contradicted by that probe. Nothing here shows that a third party can steer a builder fee, and nothing disproves it either.
evidence: static: PUSH1 0x27; PUSH1 0x20; MSTORE; KECCAK256; SLOAD; SSTORE at 0x32b6 inside body 0x2792e706, with the key loaded from memory at 0x180 + the argument index and masked to 160 bits at 0x32a6
CLOSE_TYPEHASH assertion in this script (constant present and hash-matched in both the pinned and the set-2 runtime)

peer exact-runtime rows L2-D1-06 and L2-D2-04 in atlas/block_48902346/live2_intents.json (unsigned trailing word accepted, credit key unchanged; sweep family and open leave slot 39 untouched; fee-paying shapes not run)
findings.missing_observation: A fee-paying close traced on set 2, to name the memory word the credit keys on.

findings.title: 0xd970fad5 is an owner-only accrual reassignment, not a claim and not a slot-38 debit
findings.precondition: Exchange slot 39 is an address-keyed balance mapping; slot 0 bits 16..175 hold the owner.

findings.title: The set-2 Exchange depends on a set-2-only SessionKeyManager entry, so one proxy cannot be upgraded alone
findings.angle: C1 new selectors on unaudited code; C4 upgrade route
findings.actor: whoever installs a single implementation (the timelock, through the ProxyAdmin)
findings.precondition: The set-2 close path (0x2792e706) makes a staticcall to SessionKeyManager selector 0xd95208cd before it touches a position, after a non-static call to 0xb002b9fa.
findings.trigger: Install the set-2 Exchange implementation behind a SessionKeyManager that still dispatches the pinned implementation, then attempt a signed close.
findings.impact: A direct signed close call reverts with empty revert data: the trace shows 0x6cd56616::2792e706 -> 0x8326eb88::b002b9fa (non-static, succeeds) then 0x8326eb88::d95208cd [staticcall] -> delegatecall into the pinned 0x8a5069fe -> Revert, bubbled back out. The identical constructed close succeeds with the set-2 SessionKeyManager and writes 12 Exchange slots. The failure mode through a batch is different in appearance only: replaying the historical BatchExecutor batch verbatim, the outer call succeeds under either SessionKeyManager, but with the pinned one the batch writes 4 Exchange slots and both historical positions are STILL ACTIVE, while with the set-2 one it writes 22 and closes both. So the batch wrapper masks the inner close failure rather than the Exchange tolerating a failed verifier: nothing is closed and no position state advances. The pair is only coherent together, so any single-proxy retrofit breaks closes, and a recovery candidate that delegates to the pinned Exchange implementation must be paired with the pinned SessionKeyManager. The hazard is not limited to closes: a mixed pair also changes what counts as a successful deposit sweep (row L2A-20).
evidence: artifacts/live2_authority/close_coupling.json: direct close with the pinned SessionKeyManager reverts and writes 0 slots, with the set-2 one succeeds and writes 12; the historical batch writes 4 slots with 2 positions still active under the pinned SessionKeyManager and 22 slots with 0 active under the set-2 one
artifacts/live2_authority/CloseCouplingLocal.t.sol (regenerate with python3 scripts/audit_live2_authority.py --close-coupling)
negative control inside the harness: the pinned-SessionKeyManager run must fail and write nothing
findings.missing_observation: A close replayed on set-2-era state rather than the pinned prestate, to confirm the dependency on chain state and not only on the pinned storage layout; and whether any batch item other than the closes can reach the verifier call.

findings.title: A mixed implementation pair also changes sweep success semantics, silently
findings.actor: whoever installs one implementation without the other; a deposit proxy operator
findings.precondition: A deposit proxy holds a dust pending sweep below the 10 USDC minimum; the Exchange side carries a mixed pair.
findings.trigger: A dust retry under the set-2 Exchange clears the pending word and returns success, while the pinned implementation rewrites the word with the full observed balance and reverts SweepBelowMinimum (0x329c2b0f, hash-verified here).
findings.impact: The coupling hazard is not confined to signed closes: a mixed pair also changes whether a dust sweep retry succeeds or reverts, with no revert to tell the caller that the semantics changed. The related credit question — the finalize credit follows the stored snapshot rather than the delivered amount, so a Core-side fee or partial send becomes an Exchange liability equal to the shortfall — is recorded by the signed-intents lane as plausible_unproven and matters directly to the two live PT-01 pending sweeps.
evidence: cross-referenced, not reproduced here: atlas/block_48902346/live2_intents.json rows L2-D4-02 (exact-runtime differential on both implementations plus saved fork diffs: the pinned dust retry reverts selector 849095439, the set-2 retry stores 0x24e160300 and clears) and L2-D5-01
independent check made here: 849095439 = 0x329c2b0f = keccak('SweepBelowMinimum()')[:10], asserted in this script
row L2A-15 for the same silent-masking shape on the close path
findings.missing_observation: I did not re-run the sweep differential in my own harness; reproducing it there (deposit proxy + Exchange prestate) and observing one fee-paying set-2 sweep live would close both halves.

findings.title: PAPER and Staking privilege: all admin pointers are owner-only and no owner route redirects assets
findings.precondition: PAPER owner slot 3, minter slot 4, autoApprovedSpender slot 5, stakingContract slot 9; Staking owner slot 15, packed executor slot 16.
findings.trigger: setMinter / setStakingContract / setAutoApprovedSpender / transferOwnership on PAPER; setAuthorizedExecutor / transferOwnership on Staking
findings.impact: Every one of these is owner-only (outsider reverts NotOwner 0x30cd7471) and the owner is the timelock, so no unprivileged path changes the transfer-eligibility slot or the staking pointers. The Staking owner's only lever is the authorized executor, which relays per-user signed intents, so it cannot move a user's funds without that user's signature.
